title: Ignite 2026: Windows baseline protection gives one security yes/no
summary: Microsoft put Windows baseline protection into preview through the Windows Insider Program, with general availability planned for 2027; the Book of News calls it private preview, so treat availability as not verified. It combines eight existing protections into one versioned, hardware-attested true/false device state: security processor (TPM), Secure Boot, virtualization-based security, memory integrity, signed drivers only, Windows-certified drivers, kernel debugger protection and vulnerable driver protection. The state is checked at boot and exposed as a simple query, a report of missing criteria and an attestation token for relying parties. Admins report on and enforce it through Intune compliance and baseline security mode in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
why: Today you check these settings one by one, often with different tools. A single attested signal is easier to use in compliance and Conditional Access, but it is all-or-nothing: one missing control, such as memory integrity blocked by an old driver or VBS conflicting with third-party hypervisors, makes the device fail.
todo: Do now: report on the eight criteria across your fleet today (Secure Boot, TPM, VBS, HVCI/memory integrity, vulnerable driver blocklist) so you know how many devices would fail.
Find the blockers: legacy drivers that stop memory integrity, and devs or labs that rely on non-Hyper-V virtualization.
Wait: do not build Conditional Access on the new signal until it is GA and visible in your Intune tenant. Announced and in preview, not verified in production tenants.
effective_note: Preview (Windows Insider Program); GA planned for 2027.
